newsitem.title: USA: ABC poll shows Clinton lead rising to 11 points.
newsitem.headline: ABC poll shows Clinton lead rising to 11 points.

text.p: President Bill Clinton widened his lead over Republican challenger Bob Dole to 11 points, with Dole's support falling away after a bounce from Wednesday's debate, an ABC news poll showed on Saturday.
The latest ABC poll, using a two-day Thursday-Friday average, showed Clinton's backing rose by two points, to 52 percent, while Dole's rose by one, to 41.
"The small bounce Bob Dole got following his tougher words this week (in the presidential debate) about Bill Clinton has not continued," the tracking poll said.
It said Clinton had averaged 52 percent since Labor Day. Dole's 41 points was 2 percent above his post-Labor Day average.
Reform Party candidate Ross Perot continued to trail the presidential field with 5 percent of the vote.
The poll canvassed 1,351 people, including 1,020 registered voters and 703 likely voters. The margin of error was 3.5 percent for registered voters and 4.5 percent for likely voters.
A Newsweek poll of 755 registered voters showed that if elections were held today 54 percent would vote for Clinton, 28 percent for Dole and seven percent for Perot.
The daily Reuters tracking poll on Saturday showed Clinton ahead of Dole 44.6 to 36.8 percent with 5.1 percent support for Perot.
